summary: Eric P. Hamp was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Tome School, Amherst College (~1938–1942), and Harvard University (~1946–1954), later holding posts at the University of Michigan (~1950–1951) and the University of Chicago (~1953–1991).
Eric Reinders works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied under mentors Allan G. Grapard and William F. Powell.

Eric Stephen Goodell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned MAs from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia (attested 2012), where he studied under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner.

Erich Frauwallner worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. After earning his doctoral thesis at the University of Vienna (1918–1921), he held posts there from 1928 to 1964 as director, editor, and professor.

Erich Haenisch studied under Wilhelm Grube at the University of Berlin (~1900–1904, 1913). He held sinology and East Asian philology posts at the University of Berlin (1913, 1920, 1932), Leipzig (~1925–1932), Göttingen (1925), and Munich (1927–1951).

Erich Heintel was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna (~1931–1940 for his Dr. phil. and Habilitation). He held posts there as extraordinary (1952) and ordinary professor of philosophy (1960–1982).

Erich Rudolf Jaensch was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Breslau (~1903–1905), Göttingen (~1905–1908), and Strasbourg (~1909–1910). He held posts at Halle (1912–1913), Halle-Wittenberg (~1910–1913), and Marburg (1913).

Erich Schmidt was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at Graz (~1871–1872), Strasbourg under Wilhelm Scherer (~1872–1874), and Jena (~1874–1875), and held posts at Würzburg (~1875–1877), Vienna (~1880–1887), and Berlin (~1887–1913).

Erik Braun is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Janet Gyatso, as well as Jonathan Evans, John Okell, and Saw Tun, and held a post at Harvard (attested 2010).

Erik Erikson studied at the University of Oxford and held academic posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1939–1950), the University of Pittsburgh (~1951–1960), and Harvard University (~1960–1970).

Erik Haarh studied at the University of Copenhagen (degree attested 1969) and taught there in 1955. A scholar of Tibetology and linguistics, he held posts at the Royal Danish Library (1956, 1962) and Aarhus University (1969, 1983–1993).

Erik J. Hammerstrom is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Indiana University and held an assistant professorship of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).
Erik Pema Kunsang is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has served as director of Rangjung Yeshe Publications (~1981) and as resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark.

Erik Zürcher, a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies, studied at Leiden University (~1947–1959) and under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak, Paul Demiéville, Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and Édouard Chavannes. He served as Leiden University's director (1961–1993).

Erik-Jan Zürcher studied at Het Rijnlands Lyceum Oegstgeest and Leiden University (BA ~1971–1974; PhD ~1977–1984). In history, he held posts at Radboud University (1977–1997), the International Institute of Social History (1990–1999, 2008–2012), and Leiden (1997).

Erling von Mende is a sinologist who studied law at Hamburg and Freiburg, followed by sinology at Bonn and Cologne (PhD 1964–1969, Habilitation –1979). He served as professor of sinology at the Free University of Berlin (1983–2007).
Ernest Arthur Gardner was an archaeologist who studied at Gonville and Caius College (~1880–1884). He later held a post at the University of London from 1924 to 1926.

Ernest Bender was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Temple University (~1937–1941) and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Zellig Harris, and Henry M. Hoenigswald. He held faculty posts at Penn from 1950 to 1989.

Ernest Francisco Fenollosa studied at Harvard College (~1870–1874) and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (~1876–1877). A scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and archaeology, he held posts at the University of Tokyo (1878) and Boston's MFA (1890–1896).

Ernest John Henry Mackay studied at Bristol Grammar School and the University of Bristol. In archaeology and Indology, he served as Custodian of Antiquities in Mandatory Palestine (1919–1922) and Special Officer for Exploration with the Archaeological Survey of India (~1926–1932).
